### First Mid Bank & Trust Shares Tips for Managing Holiday Spending Amid Rising Costs


November 10, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/386638223/files/doc_news/2026/Nov/10/Press-Release-First-Mid-Bank-Trust-Shares-Tips-for-Managing-Holiday-Spending-Amid-Rising-Costs.pdf)


#### *Planning ahead and accounting for more than gifts can help consumers stay on budget throughout the holiday season*


**St. Louis, MO (November 10, 2026)** Financial experts say a little extra planning this holiday season can help families account for everyday costs while keeping gifts, travel, and celebrations enjoyable.


According to First Mid Bank & Trust Chief Retail Banking Officer Stas Wolak, holiday costs extend well beyond presents. A full grocery cart for a family meal, a few tanks of gas, higher utility use, plane tickets, restaurant tabs, decorations, shipping charges, and wrapping supplies can often rival the gift budget.


“Before the first gift is purchased, inflation has already taken a seat at the holiday table. The biggest financial surprise during the holidays is often not what people buy for others – it’s all the additional expenses that come with celebrating,” Wolak said. “None of these expenses look overwhelming by themselves. Together, they can turn December into the most expensive month of the year and make January feel about three months long.”


Wolak said rising prices should not eliminate the fun and excitement of the holidays. Instead, he suggests people build one complete holiday budget, rather than just a gift budget.


“Start with the amount your household can spend without carrying a balance into the new year. Then divide that total amongst gifts, meals, travel, entertainment, decorations, charitable giving, and a small emergency fund for surprises,” Wolak explained. “If the categories add up to more than the available cash, adjust the plan before the shopping begins.”


Some of the top spending categories impacted by inflation are food and travel. Wolak suggests planning holiday menus around weekly specials, purchasing shelf-stable ingredients early, estimating fuel costs and mileage, and comparing the costs of driving and flying.


Wolak’s final tip to keeping the holidays stress-free is to track spending as it happens, whether it’s through a budgeting app, spreadsheet, or a note on your phone. He emphasized tracking even small purchases, such as coffee, because these easy-to-overlook expenses can add up quickly.


“The goal is not to eliminate generosity or fun; it’s to spend with enough purpose that the season does not compete with rent, groceries, or savings goals,” Wolak said. “When families account for the extras, make trade-offs early, and focus on the traditions that matter most, they can enjoy the holidays now without paying for them well into the new year.”


To help families track spending throughout the season, First Mid has created a holiday budget tracker accessible to anyone[here](https://www.firstmid.com/assets/files/aC7WlZdP/First%20Mid%20Holiday%20Shopping%20Tracker.xlsx?utm_source=press_release&utm_medium=investor_relations&utm_campaign=Holiday_Shopping_Tracker&utm_id=Holiday_Shopping_Tracker) .
